html:
The two-day weekend is the habit of resting on both Saturday and Sunday. It began in factories in the United States in the early twentieth century and became normal across much of the world by the 1950s.

Sunday rest was old, rooted in Christian practice. A Saturday half-day spread in Britain in the 1800s. The full Saturday off came later. A New England mill is said to have given its Jewish workers Saturday off around 1908, so that both Sabbaths were kept. In 1926 Henry Ford moved his car plants to a five-day, 40-hour week with no cut in pay. He argued that workers with free time would also buy cars.

Unions had pushed for shorter hours since the eight-hour day campaigns. The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 made the 40-hour week the legal norm in the United States, and after the Second World War most of Europe and North America followed.

The Soviet Union tried a very different week in 1929.
sum: The two-day weekend is the habit of resting on both Saturday and Sunday. It began in factories in the United States in the early twentieth century and became normal across much of the world by the 1950s.
